options: A single physical dimension table that a fact table references more than once, each reference representing a distinct business role
A dimension table that changes its column structure depending on who queries it
A fact table disguised as a dimension table
A dimension that is deleted and recreated every time the ETL process runs
questions.explain: Order date, ship date, and delivery date on a sales fact table are three distinct roles, but they can all reference one single physical Date dimension table.

questions.q: In the Microsoft Fabric example, how does the Airport dimension relate to the Flight fact table?
options: It's related twice — once as the Departure Airport, once as the Arrival Airport — using one physical Airport table
There are two separate physical Airport tables, one for departures and one for arrivals
The Airport dimension is not related to the Flight fact table at all
Airport is a fact table, not a dimension, in this example
questions.explain: This mirrors the date-dimension example with a different business: one physical Airport dimension plays two distinct roles on the same fact table.

questions.q: Why should you build only ONE physical copy of a role-playing dimension, rather than one copy per role?
options: Duplicating it means multiple ETL loads to keep in sync, more storage, and the risk that supposedly identical copies drift out of sync
SQL Server enforces a hard limit of one physical table per dimension name
Duplicate dimension tables are illegal to create in Fabric Warehouse
It has no real downside — duplicating role-playing dimensions is actually the recommended practice
questions.explain: One physical Date table avoids the maintenance and consistency problems that come from maintaining, say, three separate but supposedly identical date dimensions.

questions.q: By default, how many relationships between a role-playing dimension and a fact table can be "active" for filtering in a semantic model at once?
options: Only one — the others exist but stay inactive unless explicitly activated
All of them are always active simultaneously
None — role-playing relationships can never be active
Exactly two, no matter how many roles exist
questions.explain: A DAX measure can activate a normally-inactive relationship with USERELATIONSHIP, or the modeler can create named role-specific copies in the semantic layer, but the warehouse itself keeps just one physical table.

questions.q: Which of these is the classic, most common role-playing dimension in a data warehouse?
options: The Date dimension, serving as order date, ship date, and delivery date on the same fact table
The Product dimension
The Customer dimension
A junk dimension
questions.explain: A sales fact table almost always needs more than one date perspective, and there's no reason to build separate Date tables for each — one physical Date dimension plays all the roles.
